extraction.name: NWPU-RESISC45
extraction.description: NWPU-RESISC45 is a large-scale publicly available benchmark dataset for Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification (RESISC), created by Northwestern Polytechnical University (NWPU). It contains 31,500 RGB images covering 45 scene classes with 700 images per class, at a size of 256×256 pixels, with spatial resolution varying from about 30 m to 0.2 m per pixel. The dataset features rich image variations in translation, spatial resolution, viewpoint, object pose, illumination, background, and occlusion, and covers more than 100 countries and regions worldwide.
extraction.creator: Gong Cheng (Northwestern Polytechnical University); Junwei Han (Northwestern Polytechnical University); Xiaoqiang Lu (Xi'an Institute of Optics and Precision Mechanics, Chinese Academy of Sciences)
extraction.citeAs: G. Cheng, J. Han, and X. Lu, "Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification: Benchmark and State of the Art," Proceedings of the IEEE, 2017.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were manually extracted from Google Earth (Google Inc.) by experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation. Scene classes were selected by investigating existing datasets and searching keywords on Web of Science and Google Scholar. Images were carefully selected under all kinds of weathers, seasons, illumination conditions, imaging conditions, and scales to ensure rich variations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Google Earth (Google Inc.), which maps the Earth by the superimposition of images obtained from satellite imagery, aerial photography, and geographic information system (GIS) onto a 3D globe. The 31,500 images cover more than 100 countries and regions all over the world.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Images were extracted from Google Earth by experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation. Scene classes were selected by investigating existing datasets and searching keywords on Web of Science and Google Scholar. For the Brazilian Coffee Scene dataset, identification of coffee crops was performed manually by agricultural researchers, with tiles having at least 85% coffee pixels assigned to the coffee class and tiles with less than 10% coffee pixels assigned to the non-coffee class.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Almost all existing datasets have limitations including small scale of scene classes and image numbers, lack of image variations and diversity, and saturation of accuracy; the SIRI-WHU dataset mainly covers urban areas in China and hence lacks diversity; the Brazilian Coffee Scene dataset has only two scene classes, which is quite small for testing multi-class scene classification methods; the WHU-RS19 dataset has a relatively small number of images per class
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Developing and evaluating data-driven algorithms for remote sensing image scene classification; training and evaluation of deep learning-based methods; performance benchmarking of scene classification approaches; applications including natural hazards detection, land use and land cover determination, geospatial object detection, geographic image retrieval, vegetation mapping, environment monitoring, and urban planning
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were extracted from Google Earth by experts in remote sensing image interpretation. For the Brazilian Coffee Scene dataset, tiles with at least 85% coffee pixels were assigned to the coffee class and tiles with less than 10% coffee pixels were assigned to the non-coffee class. For the NWPU-RESISC45 dataset, images were carefully selected under all kinds of weathers, seasons, illumination conditions, imaging conditions, and scales. Scene classes were selected by investigating existing datasets and searching relevant keywords on Web of Science and Google Scholar. All images are 256x256 pixels in RGB color space.
